The note proves real/complex generic-identification equivalence for depth-one graphs and graphs with shallow Tian components, plus necessary conditions on any separator. It neither constructs a separator nor excludes all depth-two graphs, so the requested minimum depth remains undetermined.

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the depth-one equivalence, a shallow Tian-component obstruction, a parity filter, and a four-vertex necessary bound; its mathematical referee passed, and the cited FDD12 decomposition was verified from Theorem 9. The accepted topic required resolving the minimal depth, but neither a certified depth-two separator nor a universal depth-two no-go theorem was obtained. An independent validity gate confirmed that narrowing to the sound shallow result would require a fresh proposal rather than continuing this qid.
tldr: The headline result is a complete quadratic-fiber obstruction: for every acyclic mixed graph of directed depth at most one, real generic identification on the full positive-definite domain is equivalent to complex generic degree one. The same equivalence holds when every Tian mixed component has depth at most one, even if the full graph is deeper; a linear-time graph test recognizes this class. Any real/complex separator has at least four vertices, finite odd complex degree at least three, and an internal directed length-two path in a Tian component. Whether one exists at depth two is an open sharpness frontier.
gap: Odd complex degree can theoretically leave one real point, but the first possible directed depth in the unrestricted positive-definite acyclic model is unknown.
